name: Gemini agent
why: NEW: one work agent that plans a job, spins up sub-agents with their own Workspace identities, and connects to Microsoft 365, Slack, Jira and Snowflake; it routes work across more than one model family. Businesses first, consumers later.

name: Agents API (public beta)
why: NEW: hosted agent execution with memory, tools and multi-agent support, announced at DevDay. Moves agent runtimes from developers’ own servers onto OpenAI’s platform.

name: Agentforce long-horizon runtime
why: NEW at Dreamforce: agents that pursue a goal over days or weeks, an orchestrating ‘Superagent’, and risk scores for MCP servers. Several parts are pilot or beta only.

name: Temporal
why: NEW raise: durable-execution platform that keeps long-running agent workflows alive through failures and restarts — the plumbing under many production agents. Bloomberg had reported talks at about $500M in August; the closed round was larger.

name: Nous Research (Hermes Agent)
why: NEW raise: open-model lab behind the Hermes Agent framework.

name: AIR
why: NEW raise: vets the skills and add-ons that agents install, a security layer for the agent supply chain.

name: OpenAI Agent Plugins
why: UPDATED: the interoperability standard for agent tool-calling gained a Plugin Creator and a revised submission process at DevDay (29 Sep). First announced early August.

name: Ruflo (Claude Flow)
why: Meta-harness that turns coding agents into self-learning multi-agent swarms with vector memory and 100+ specialist agents. Star count is the 11 August snapshot; it was not re-read this refresh.

name: Cursor Origin
why: NEW: git hosting built into the Cursor editor, with pull requests, GitHub mirroring and CI through Vercel, Depot and Buildkite — the first direct challenge to GitHub from an AI-editor company.

name: Codex Cloud & Codex Security Cloud
why: NEW at DevDay: Codex Cloud keeps coding tasks running after the laptop closes; Security Cloud runs scheduled vulnerability scans; an ‘Ultrafast’ paid tier claims up to 8x faster generation. Replaces the July price-cut item on this board.

name: Google Antigravity
why: UPDATED: the agentic IDE’s SDK added support for local models (Gemma 4 and OpenAI-compatible servers) on 23 September, so teams can run it without sending code to a hosted model.

name: Muse Code
why: Terminal coding agent for large repositories (beta since August), now alongside Meta’s consumer Muse agent. No new developer release found this window.

name: Graphify
why: Turns a folder of code, docs, papers or images into a queryable knowledge graph for coding assistants. Still nascent; star count is the 11 August snapshot.

name: GPT-6 Astra
why: NEW flagship, priced at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens, and the first OpenAI model rated ‘Critical’ for cyber capability, so rollout was staged. GPT-6 Sol and Luna followed on 22 Sep and GPT-6 reached all ChatGPT users on 7 Oct.

name: Gemini 4 Argon
why: NEW: Google’s most capable model, released first only to the 650+ partners in its Fairwind cyber-defence programme; no public release date yet.

name: Grok 4.7
why: NEW: a model aimed at long-running agentic coding, built jointly with Cursor and launched inside Cursor the same day.

name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
why: NEW open weights (MIT): 552B total parameters, a small active set, 1M context, and a much smaller KV cache that cuts serving cost. Supersedes V4-Flash on this board.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
why: NEW open-weight preview of the Qwen4 architecture, under a community licence rather than Apache.

name: Qwen3.8-Max (open weights)
why: UPDATED: the promised open weights shipped as Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (2.4T parameters, 95B active) under a custom licence. The open version is text-only with 262K context; 1M context and vision stay API-only, and firms with over $50M revenue need a separate licence.

name: Muse personal agent
why: NEW consumer agent for iOS, Android and the web at $20 and $100 a month; reached No. 2 on the US App Store, with Mac, iPad and a small-business version following.

name: Dots
why: NEW always-on personal agents, each with its own cloud computer, running on GPT-6 Astra. Who gets it first differs by source (Pro and Business Premium per CNBC; Pro outside the EEA, Switzerland and the UK per OpenAI’s forum).

name: Gemini Spark
why: UPDATED: the persistent cloud agent can now act in Google Photos (4 Sep) and take delegated tasks from the Gemini app for Windows. The $99.99/mo AI Ultra price is still reported, not first-party.

name: GitHub Copilot (unified)
why: UPDATED: GitHub is merging Copilot Chat on github.com, Copilot in GitHub Mobile and the Copilot cloud agent into one Copilot experience from late September, per its changelog of 28 August.

name: Copilot Autopilot
why: NEW in the ‘new Copilot’: a proactive agent (formerly Scout) that runs recurring work and follows up on threads without being prompted; private preview from the end of September.

name: UiPath Maestro Flow + voice agents
why: NEW: Maestro Flow is generally available, with chat and real-time phone agents in preview that take inbound calls and place outbound ones inside automation flows.

name: Cloudflare Kitesurf
why: UPDATED: the agent-first cloud browser added WebMCP and terminal rendering on 28 September; open-sourcing is still ‘coming soon’.

name: Cloudflare Wallets & cloudflare.pay
why: Gives AI agents an identity plus controlled spending via stablecoins, with per-agent caps on transaction size and approved merchants. No new development found this window.
